data.text:
Bridge Between Chakhabama And Kikruma Declared Unsafe For Heavy Vehicles

𝐊𝐨𝐡𝐢𝐦𝐚, 𝐀𝐮𝐠 𝟐𝟐 (𝐖𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐍𝐀𝐆𝐀𝐒): Traffic movement has been severely disrupted after damages were reported on the bridge connecting Chakhabama and Kikruma under PKG-2 (Kohima–Jessami Road, NH-29). Authorities have completely restricted the movement of heavy and medium vehicles carrying loads above 5 metric tons with immediate effect until further notice.

The bridge developed cracks and surface damage, exposing reinforcement bars beneath. Officials cordoned off the affected section and placed safety markers to prevent accidents. As a result, several trucks have been stranded on both sides of the route. Light vehicles are still being allowed to pass cautiously.

In an official traffic advisory issued by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Phek, travelers have been advised to take alternate routes:

1. Zero Point (Chakhabama) – Chetkeba – Thuvopisu – Phek

2. Zero Point (Chakhabama) – Chetkeba – Pfutsero

The advisory has called for strict compliance as maintenance and repair work on the damaged bridge is underway.

The Chakhabama–Kikruma stretch is a vital lifeline for southern Nagaland, and prolonged restrictions could hamper the transportation of essential goods. Commuters and truck operators have urged authorities for urgent repairs to restore smooth traffic flow.

data.text:
Urban flooding in Karachi – a reality we must face together

Every monsoon, #Karachi faces #urbanflooding, and every time, fingers are pointed at #PPP and #ChairmanPPP Bilawal Bhutto Zardari. But is this issue really about one party, or is it bigger than politics?

Urban flooding is a global phenomenon. Cities like #Jakarta, #Bangkok, #Manila, #Houston, #NewYork, #London,and #Cologne face the same problem. Even within #Pakistan, #Lahore, #Rawalpindi, #Peshawar, #Quetta, and #Multan have seen severe urban flooding. This isn’t a Karachi-only story.

#Karachi is a #mega-city of over 20 million people. Its population keeps growing, making it nearly impossible to install an entirely new sewerage and drainage system overnight. PPP has taken preventive measures, but no drainage system in the world can function if it’s blocked with garbage.

So here’s the question: while everyone is quick to #slam the #government, what are we as citizens doing for our city?

Are we #disposing of #garbage properly?

Are we stopping others from #dumping #waste in #drains?

Are we #holding ourselves #accountable, not just #politicians?

Urban flooding is not just the failure of any government, it’s a shared failure of planning, enforcement, and civic responsibility. If Karachi is to be flood-free, every citizen must play their part alongside the government.

It’s easy to #blame #PPP, but harder to admit: when drains are full of garbage, who put it there?

#KarachiFloods 
#SharedResponsibility 
#StopBlamingStartCleaning 
#KarachiWithPPP
